subject: Post-call: model-fit benchmarking kit & next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@carebridge.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@carebridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model-fit benchmarking kit & next steps

Hi Amit / Lena —

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a pragmatic plan to validate model fit on Redwood:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: triage assistant that classifies incoming messages and suggests one of 12 standardized dispositions.
- SLA goals: p95 latency < 350ms for single-turn suggestions; batch scoring for nightly re-runs ok.
- Data: ~350k historical triage examples (labels are noisy, ~85% agreement), and a small curated prompt set (~120 cases) for quality checks.

Recommended quick validation approach (3-step kit)
1) Smoke-run: run 500 representative examples through two model families to confirm latency and basic label alignment.
2) Bench scoring: run the 5k holdout slice through the benchmark template (attached) to compute macro-F1, top-1 accuracy and a policy mismatch rate.
3) Prompt bank vetting: apply our prompt variants (attached) to guard against regression on edge cases you flagged (short clinical notes, multi-label messages).

Model recommendations (initial shortlist)
- Candidate A: large open decoder (FP16) — best for accuracy on long-form notes, moderate latency.
- Candidate B: quantized 8-bit distilled variant — favorable latency/cost, slightly lower recall on rare labels.
- Fallback: a small specialist reranker for the high-risk dispositions to reduce false positives.

Operational asks / next steps
- Please confirm the 5k holdout slice you want scored (example: random stratified by disposition). If you want, drop the Drive link to the CSV and we’ll validate format.
- Ben will propose an exact run configuration (batch size, qbits, timeout) once you confirm the slice.
- Proposed timeline: smoke-run by 04/09, full bench by 04/13, and kickoff call to review results w/ your PMs on 04/15.

Attachments sent: redwood_benchmark_template.csv (schema + scorer), prompt_bank_v1.md, model-recommendation-matrix.pdf

Thanks again — I’ll schedule the kickoff once I get confirmation on the holdout slice and a preferred 04/15 time window.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Amit — quick answers to your technical questions.

1) 6k holdout: fine to run the full 6k. We usually validate format first and then run a quick schema check (headers: id, text, gold_label, channel, timestamp). If there are PII columns beyond text, mark them and we can redact before benching.

2) Reranker: yes — implemented as a second-pass. Typical flow: base model -> top-N candidates -> reranker scores and adjusts top-1. The extra latency depends on N and whether the reranker is half-precision quantized. For a top-5 rerank on our quantized reranker you’re looking at ~70-120ms additional p95 in our internal microbench. We can tune to keep combined p95 < 350ms if you prefer.

3) Data retention: We do not persist raw input beyond the bench job by default for ad-hoc evals. We snapshot ephemeral logs for debugging (48-72 hours) and destroy afterward unless you opt-in to longer retention. I’ll attach the short data-retention snippet we share with procurement.

Operational note: to keep the bench reproducible, please include a stable seed column if you have it — otherwise we’ll stratify deterministically and share the seed.

Ben
